$note: Data-processor registry, t-2026-10-03-23. Every third party that can receive personal or order data from upready-store, what it gets, why, which instance(s) may use it, and the legal basis for sending it data. docs/instances/RULES.md §2 is the prose this file backs. apps/backend/src/scripts/__tests__/processors-registry.unit.spec.ts fails CI when a payment-* or auth-* module under apps/backend/src/modules/ has no matching entry here (integrationModules below is what that test reads).

processors.whatItReceives: order amount, order id, buyer email/phone for the payment page, and the 54-FZ receipt line items (name, quantity, price, tax)
processors.why: card and SBP payment processing for RU-instance orders
processors.legalBasis: contract performance (processing the buyer's own order) — 152-FZ, no cross-border transfer

processors.whatItReceives: order amount, currency, title/description, success/fail URLs, and the webhook's own transaction identifiers
processors.why: card, Wallet Pay (TON/USDT/BTC) and SBP payment processing for INTL-instance orders
processors.legalBasis: contract performance, under a transfer basis the shop owner's own Tribute merchant agreement provides — never used on the RU instance (docs/instances/RULES.md §2)

processors.service: BTCPay Server (the shop owner's own store)
processors.country: wherever the shop owner hosts it; self-hosted open-source software, not a company
processors.whatItReceives: order amount and currency, the payment session id as the invoice's orderId, the return URL to the shop and the checkout language; the buyer's browser then opens the invoice page on that server directly. No name, email or address is sent
processors.why: cryptocurrency payments for INTL-instance orders, paid straight into the shop owner's own wallet (ask-20261005-070255-438f)
processors.legalBasis: contract performance; the server is run by the shop owner or a host the owner chose, never by the platform — never used on the RU instance, where 282-FZ Art. 1 part 6 bans accepting cryptocurrency for goods (docs/instances/RULES.md §2)

processors.whatItReceives: the buyer's Yandex account id, email and display name, returned by the OAuth callback
processors.why: "Sign in with Yandex ID" for buyers, on both instances
processors.legalBasis: the buyer's own consent, given by starting the OAuth flow — 152-FZ, no cross-border transfer for the RU instance's own buyers

processors.country: international (Telegram's operating entity is outside Russia)
processors.whatItReceives: the buyer's Telegram user id, username and display name (sign-in and Mini App), and order-status messages sent to the owner or the buyer by the shop bot
processors.why: "Sign in with Telegram", the Mini App, shop-bot order notifications and the owner's /manager channel, on both instances
processors.legalBasis: the buyer's own consent, given by using Telegram sign-in — on the RU instance this requires a consent SEPARATE from the general personal-data consent, since the recipient is outside Russia (docs/instances/RULES.md §2)

processors.country: same country as the instance's own host (RU host for ru, Contabo/Germany for intl)
processors.whatItReceives: the buyer's email address and the transactional letter's content (order confirmation, password reset)
processors.legalBasis: contract performance — no cross-border transfer, since the relay runs on the instance's own host

processors.whatItReceives: the buyer's name, phone, delivery address or pickup point, and the parcel's declared contents and value
processors.why: fulfillment: courier and pickup-point delivery quotes and labels for RU-instance orders
processors.legalBasis: contract performance (delivering the buyer's own order) — 152-FZ, no cross-border transfer

processors.whatItReceives: the buyer's name, phone, delivery address or pickup point, and the parcel's declared contents and value
processors.why: fulfillment: postal delivery quotes and labels for RU-instance orders
processors.legalBasis: contract performance (delivering the buyer's own order) — 152-FZ, no cross-border transfer

processors.whatItReceives: the buyer's delivery address or pickup point, used to resolve rates across the RU carriers it aggregates
processors.why: fulfillment: a single rate-and-label API over CDEK, Pochta Rossii and other RU carriers
processors.legalBasis: contract performance (delivering the buyer's own order) — 152-FZ, no cross-border transfer

processors.whatItReceives: nothing from a buyer directly — the shop's own catalog, price and stock rows are read back from Wildberries into the mirror tables this module owns
processors.why: read-only sync of the shop's existing Wildberries listings (products, prices, stock, orders, feedback) into the admin panel
processors.legalBasis: the shop owner's own Wildberries seller account and API key — no buyer personal data leaves upready-store for this integration

processors.whatItReceives: the shop's own catalog, price and stock rows, and order data for orders placed on Ozon's own marketplace
processors.why: marketplace sync of the shop's existing Ozon listings and orders into the admin panel
processors.legalBasis: the shop owner's own Ozon seller account and API key

processors.whatItReceives: storefront visitor and session data (pageviews, events) for whichever tenant has saved a GA4 measurement id
processors.legalBasis: forbidden on the RU instance (docs/instances/RULES.md §2); on INTL, the tenant's own consent banner and a GDPR-compliant configuration (consent mode / IP anonymisation) are the shop owner's responsibility, not this module's

processors.whatItReceives: storefront visitor and session data (pageviews, events) for whichever tenant has saved a counter id
processors.why: storefront traffic analytics, tenant-configured (t17-analytics); the only analytics counter allowed on the RU instance
processors.legalBasis: contract performance / tenant's own configuration — works outside Russia too, per the plan's own note
